check: the final report write cannot turn a failed profile into a passing one
why: Twenty hours of profile are only worth anything if the verdict survives being written and read. A write failure that produced a silent pass would waste the run and, worse, certify it.

pathIsWritable.note: The checkpoints are already being written there, so the directory is proven writable by 407 successful writes rather than by a probe alone.

failClosed: writeReport throwing IOException is caught, and the handler sets passed = false alongside recording the failure, so a report that cannot be written cannot be reported as a pass.
The handler then halts the server when passed is false, with the comment that a halted or failed profile must not look like a completed one.
If the write fails there is no report file at all, so Test-S5Stress.ps1 finds none, sets reportPassed false, and refuses. The gate that reads the report therefore backstops the fixture's own verdict.
conclusion: Every path from a failed profile leads to a refusal. There is no route by which a write problem yields a pass.
